    <title>v1.64.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>🧰 WebMCP</h2>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-webmcp" rel="nofollow">page.webmcp</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-frame#frame-webmcp" rel="nofollow">frame.webmcp</a> give access to the tools that a page registers through<br>
the experimental <a href="https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/" rel="nofollow">WebMCP</a> browser API, so you can test them like<br>
any other part of your app:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="browser = chromium.launch(args=[&quot;--enable-features=WebMCP&quot;])
page = browser.new_page()
page.goto(&quot;https://example.com&quot;)

for tool in page.webmcp.tools():
    print(tool[&quot;name&quot;], tool[&quot;description&quot;])

result = page.webmcp.call_tool(&quot;add&quot;, {&quot;a&quot;: 2, &quot;b&quot;: 40})
print(result[&quot;content&quot;][0][&quot;text&quot;])  # &quot;42&quot;"><pre><span class="pl-s1">browser</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">chromium</span>.<span class="pl-c1">launch</span>(<span class="pl-s1">args</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>[<span class="pl-s">"--enable-features=WebMCP"</span>])
<span class="pl-s1">page</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">browser</span>.<span class="pl-c1">new_page</span>()
<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">goto</span>(<span class="pl-s">"https://example.com"</span>)

<span class="pl-k">for</span> <span class="pl-s1">tool</span> <span class="pl-c1">in</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">webmcp</span>.<span class="pl-c1">tools</span>():
    <span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s1">tool</span>[<span class="pl-s">"name"</span>], <span class="pl-s1">tool</span>[<span class="pl-s">"description"</span>])

<span class="pl-s1">result</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">webmcp</span>.<span class="pl-c1">call_tool</span>(<span class="pl-s">"add"</span>, {<span class="pl-s">"a"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">2</span>, <span class="pl-s">"b"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">40</span>})
<span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s1">result</span>[<span class="pl-s">"content"</span>][<span class="pl-c1">0</span>][<span class="pl-s">"text"</span>])  <span class="pl-c"># "42"</span></pre></div>
<p><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/getting-started-mcp" rel="nofollow">Playwright MCP</a> also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as <code>webmcp_&lt;tool&gt;</code>. Pass <code>--no-webmcp</code> to opt out.</p>
<p><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/getting-started-cli" rel="nofollow"><code>playwright-cli</code></a> exposes them as well:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{&quot;query&quot;:&quot;cats&quot;}'"><pre>playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>{"query":"cats"}<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span></pre></div>
<h2>🎬 Better videos</h2>
<p>Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.screencast.start(path=&quot;video.webm&quot;, size={&quot;width&quot;: 1920, &quot;height&quot;: 1080}, fps=60)
page.screencast.show_actions(
    style={
        &quot;point&quot;: &quot;width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: red&quot;,
        &quot;highlight&quot;: &quot;outline: 2px solid #333; background: rgba(0, 128, 255, .15)&quot;,
        &quot;title&quot;: &quot;font-size: 16px&quot;,
    }
)"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">start</span>(<span class="pl-s1">path</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"video.webm"</span>, <span class="pl-s1">size</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>{<span class="pl-s">"width"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">1920</span>, <span class="pl-s">"height"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">1080</span>}, <span class="pl-s1">fps</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">60</span>)
<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">show_actions</span>(
    <span class="pl-s1">style</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>{
        <span class="pl-s">"point"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: red"</span>,
        <span class="pl-s">"highlight"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"outline: 2px solid #333; background: rgba(0, 128, 255, .15)"</span>,
        <span class="pl-s">"title"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"font-size: 16px"</span>,
    }
)</pre></div>
<ul>
<li>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context-option-record-video-fps" rel="nofollow"><code>record_video_fps</code></a> option and new <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-start-option-fps" rel="nofollow"><code>fps</code></a> option in<br>
<a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-start" rel="nofollow">screencast.start()</a>. Firefox and WebKit currently capture up to 25 frames per second.</li>
<li>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-actions-option-style" rel="nofollow"><code>style</code></a> option takes CSS declarations for the <code>point</code> marker, the target<br>
<code>highlight</code> and the action <code>title</code>. It replaces the <code>font_size</code> option, which is now deprecated.</li>
<li>The cursor stays visible at the last action point, survives navigations and travels along a natural, eased path.</li>
<li>Videos are encoded with VP9 instead of VP8, which takes less CPU and produces smaller files of the same or better<br>
quality.</li>
<li>All video options are also available in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/getting-started-mcp" rel="nofollow">Playwright MCP</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/getting-started-cli" rel="nofollow"><code>playwright-cli</code></a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2>🪆 Locator.within()</h2>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-within" rel="nofollow">locator.within()</a> combines two locators that you already have, reading in the natural order —<br>
"this button, within that dialog":</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="save_button = page.get_by_role(&quot;button&quot;, name=&quot;Save&quot;)
dialog = page.get_by_test_id(&quot;settings-dialog&quot;)

save_button.within(dialog).click()"><pre><span class="pl-s1">save_button</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">get_by_role</span>(<span class="pl-s">"button"</span>, <span class="pl-s1">name</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"Save"</span>)
<span class="pl-s1">dialog</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">get_by_test_id</span>(<span class="pl-s">"settings-dialog"</span>)

<span class="pl-s1">save_button</span>.<span class="pl-c1">within</span>(<span class="pl-s1">dialog</span>).<span class="pl-c1">click</span>()</pre></div>
<p>Relative locators such as <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-nth" rel="nofollow">locator.nth()</a> or <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-first" rel="nofollow">locator.first</a> are resolved inside each parent<br>
separately, which makes column-like queries straightforward:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# The third cell of every row, not the third cell in the table.
third_column = page.get_by_role(&quot;cell&quot;).nth(2).within(page.get_by_role(&quot;row&quot;))
expect(third_column).to_have_text([&quot;Apple&quot;, &quot;Banana&quot;, &quot;Cherry&quot;])"><pre><span class="pl-c"># The third cell of every row, not the third cell in the table.</span>
<span class="pl-s1">third_column</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">get_by_role</span>(<span class="pl-s">"cell"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">nth</span>(<span class="pl-c1">2</span>).<span class="pl-c1">within</span>(<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">get_by_role</span>(<span class="pl-s">"row"</span>))
<span class="pl-en">expect</span>(<span class="pl-s1">third_column</span>).<span class="pl-c1">to_have_text</span>([<span class="pl-s">"Apple"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"Banana"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"Cherry"</span>])</pre></div>
<h2>New APIs</h2>
<ul>
<li>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-ref" rel="nofollow">page.get_by_ref()</a> locates an element by its aria ref, such as <code>e2</code>, reported by <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-aria-snapshot" rel="nofollow">page.aria_snapshot()</a> in the <code>"ai"</code> mode.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>New option <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-content-option-include-shadow" rel="nofollow"><code>include_shadow</code></a> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-content" rel="nofollow">page.content()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-frame#frame-content" rel="nofollow">frame.content()</a> serializes open shadow roots as <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_components/Using_shadow_DOM#declaratively_with_html" rel="nofollow">declarative shadow DOM</a>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>New option <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-credentials#credentials-create-option-sign-count" rel="nofollow"><code>sign_count</code></a> sets the initial signature counter of a virtual credential. <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-credentials#credentials-create" rel="nofollow">credentials.create()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-credentials#credentials-get" rel="nofollow">credentials.get()</a> return the current <code>sign_count</code>, and it is saved and restored together with the credentials in the storage state.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext#api-request-context-add-cookies" rel="nofollow">api_request_context.add_cookies()</a>, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext#api-request-context-cookies" rel="nofollow">api_request_context.cookies()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext#api-request-context-clear-cookies" rel="nofollow">api_request_context.clear_cookies()</a> manage cookies of a request context, mirroring the <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext" rel="nofollow">BrowserContext</a> methods:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="request.add_cookies(
    [{&quot;name&quot;: &quot;session-id&quot;, &quot;value&quot;: &quot;42&quot;, &quot;url&quot;: &quot;https://example.com&quot;}]
)
print(request.cookies(&quot;https://example.com&quot;))
request.clear_cookies(name=&quot;session-id&quot;)"><pre><span class="pl-s1">request</span>.<span class="pl-c1">add_cookies</span>(
    [{<span class="pl-s">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"session-id"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"value"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"42"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"url"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"https://example.com"</span>}]
)
<span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s1">request</span>.<span class="pl-c1">cookies</span>(<span class="pl-s">"https://example.com"</span>))
<span class="pl-s1">request</span>.<span class="pl-c1">clear_cookies</span>(<span class="pl-s1">name</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"session-id"</span>)</pre></div>
</li>
</ul>
<h2>Breaking Changes <g-emoji class="g-emoji" alias="warning">⚠️</g-emoji></h2>
<ul>
<li>Elements inside hidden iframes are considered hidden. Elements inside an iframe that is not visible, for example with <code>visibility: hidden</code>, are now considered hidden by actions, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-is-visible" rel="nofollow">locator.is_visible()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locatorassertions#locator-assertions-to-be-visible" rel="nofollow">expect(locator).to_be_visible()</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Browser Versions</h2>
<ul>
<li>Chromium 156.0.8078.4</li>
<li>Mozilla Firefox 157.0</li>
<li>WebKit 27.2</li>
</ul>
<p>This version was also tested against the following stable channels:</p>
<ul>
<li>Google Chrome 155</li>
<li>Microsoft Edge 155</li>
</ul></content>

    <title>v1.63.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>🪟 Locate across frames</h2>
<p><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-frame-locator" rel="nofollow">page.frame_locator()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-frame#frame-frame-locator" rel="nofollow">frame.frame_locator()</a> called without a selector search in any frame of the<br>
subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# Finds the button in any frame on the page.
page.frame_locator().get_by_role(&quot;button&quot;).click()"><pre><span class="pl-c"># Finds the button in any frame on the page.</span>
<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">frame_locator</span>().<span class="pl-c1">get_by_role</span>(<span class="pl-s">"button"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">click</span>()</pre></div>
<p>The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it<br>
matches elements in several frames.</p>
<h2>👁️ Visible-only locators</h2>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-visible" rel="nofollow">locator.visible</a> returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended<br>
replacement for the <code>:visible</code> CSS pseudo-class:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.locator(&quot;button&quot;).visible.click()"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">locator</span>(<span class="pl-s">"button"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">visible</span>.<span class="pl-c1">click</span>()</pre></div>
<h2>🖼️ Aria and screen snapshots in traces</h2>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-start-option-aria-snapshots" rel="nofollow"><code>aria_snapshots</code></a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-start-option-screen-snapshots" rel="nofollow"><code>screen_snapshots</code></a> options of<br>
<a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-start" rel="nofollow">tracing.start()</a> capture an aria snapshot and a screenshot of the page on every action:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="context.tracing.start(snapshots=True, aria_snapshots=True, screen_snapshots=True)"><pre><span class="pl-s1">context</span>.<span class="pl-c1">tracing</span>.<span class="pl-c1">start</span>(<span class="pl-s1">snapshots</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">True</span>, <span class="pl-s1">aria_snapshots</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">True</span>, <span class="pl-s1">screen_snapshots</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">True</span>)</pre></div>
<p>With aria and screen snapshots recorded, the new <strong>Display Aria</strong> mode in the trace viewer shows the action screenshot<br>
side by side with the aria snapshot, and hovering an aria node highlights it on the screenshot.</p>
<h2>New APIs</h2>
<h3>Browser and Context</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context-option-http-credentials" rel="nofollow"><code>http_credentials</code></a> now also accepts an array of credentials. The first entry matching the request origin is used, and entries without an origin match any request.</li>
<li>New option <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-storage-state-option-opfs" rel="nofollow"><code>opfs</code></a> includes the <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/File_System_API/Origin_private_file_system" rel="nofollow">origin private file system</a> in the storage state, so it can be persisted and restored into later contexts.</li>
<li>New events <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-event-dialog-closed" rel="nofollow">page.on('dialogclosed')</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-dialog-closed" rel="nofollow">browserContext.on('dialogclosed')</a> are emitted when a JavaScript dialog is accepted, dismissed or closed by the user.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Command line</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>playwright install --no-remove</code> keeps the browsers of other Playwright installations instead of removing them.</li>
<li><code>playwright codegen --http-credentials</code> records against pages behind HTTP authentication.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Announcements</h2>
<ul>
<li><g-emoji class="g-emoji" alias="warning">⚠️</g-emoji> Ubuntu 20.04 is not supported anymore.</li>
<li>🐧 On Linux arm64, Playwright now downloads the <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing" rel="nofollow">Chrome for Testing</a> build of Chromium, the same build used on all other platforms.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Browser Versions</h2>
<ul>
<li>Chromium 153.0.8010.12</li>
<li>Mozilla Firefox 155.0</li>
<li>WebKit 26.6</li>
</ul>
<p>This version was also tested against the following stable channels:</p>
<ul>
<li>Google Chrome 153</li>
<li>Microsoft Edge 153</li>
</ul></content>

    <title>v1.62.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>🖼️ WebP screenshots</h2>
<p><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-screenshot" rel="nofollow">page.screenshot()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-screenshot" rel="nofollow">locator.screenshot()</a> can now capture screenshots in the WebP format. Playwright infers the format from a <code>.webp</code> file extension, or you can set the <code>type</code> explicitly. Quality <code>100</code> (the default) is lossless, while lower values use lossy compression:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.screenshot(path=&quot;homepage.webp&quot;, quality=50)"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screenshot</span>(<span class="pl-s1">path</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"homepage.webp"</span>, <span class="pl-s1">quality</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">50</span>)</pre></div>
<h2>New APIs</h2>
<ul>
<li>New <code>scroll</code> option (<code>"auto"</code> | <code>"none"</code>) on actions to opt out of Playwright's automatic scrolling into view.</li>
<li>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-wait-for-function" rel="nofollow">locator.wait_for_function()</a> waits until a function called with the matching element returns a truthy value.</li>
<li>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-apiresponse#api-response-timing" rel="nofollow">apiResponse.timing()</a> returns resource timing information for an API response.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Announcements</h2>
<ul>
<li>📋 The clipboard is now isolated from the operating system in headless mode, so tests that use <code>navigator.clipboard</code> no longer read or overwrite the clipboard of the machine running them.</li>
<li><g-emoji class="g-emoji" alias="warning">⚠️</g-emoji> Debian 11 is not supported anymore.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Browser Versions</h2>
<ul>
<li>Chromium 151.0.7922.34</li>
<li>Mozilla Firefox 153.0</li>
<li>WebKit 26.5</li>
</ul>
<p>This version was also tested against the following stable channels:</p>
<ul>
<li>Google Chrome 151</li>
<li>Microsoft Edge 151</li>
</ul></content>

    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-python/releases/tag/v1.61.0"/>
    <title>v1.61.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>🔑 WebAuthn passkeys</h2>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-credentials" rel="nofollow">Credentials</a> virtual authenticator, available via <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-credentials" rel="nofollow">browserContext.credentials</a>, lets tests register passkeys and answer <code>navigator.credentials.create()</code> / <code>navigator.credentials.get()</code> ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="context = browser.new_context()

# Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.
context.credentials.create(&quot;example.com&quot;,
    id=credential_id,
    user_handle=user_handle,
    private_key=private_key,
    public_key=public_key,
)
context.credentials.install()

page = context.new_page()
page.goto(&quot;https://example.com/login&quot;)
# The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey."><pre><span class="pl-s1">context</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">browser</span>.<span class="pl-c1">new_context</span>()

<span class="pl-c"># Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.</span>
<span class="pl-s1">context</span>.<span class="pl-c1">credentials</span>.<span class="pl-c1">create</span>(<span class="pl-s">"example.com"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">id</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s1">credential_id</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">user_handle</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s1">user_handle</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">private_key</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s1">private_key</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">public_key</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s1">public_key</span>,
)
<span class="pl-s1">context</span>.<span class="pl-c1">credentials</span>.<span class="pl-c1">install</span>()

<span class="pl-s1">page</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">context</span>.<span class="pl-c1">new_page</span>()
<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">goto</span>(<span class="pl-s">"https://example.com/login"</span>)
<span class="pl-c"># The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.</span></pre></div>
<p>You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-credentials#credentials-get" rel="nofollow">credentials.get()</a>, and seed it into later tests — see <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-credentials" rel="nofollow">Credentials</a> for details.</p>
<h2>🗃️ Web Storage</h2>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-webstorage" rel="nofollow">WebStorage</a> API, available via <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-local-storage" rel="nofollow">page.localStorage</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-session-storage" rel="nofollow">page.sessionStorage</a>, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.local_storage.set_item(&quot;token&quot;, &quot;abc&quot;)
token = page.local_storage.get_item(&quot;token&quot;)
items = page.session_storage.items()"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">local_storage</span>.<span class="pl-c1">set_item</span>(<span class="pl-s">"token"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"abc"</span>)
<span class="pl-s1">token</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">local_storage</span>.<span class="pl-c1">get_item</span>(<span class="pl-s">"token"</span>)
<span class="pl-s1">items</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">session_storage</span>.<span class="pl-c1">items</span>()</pre></div>
<h2>New APIs</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-apiresponse#api-response-security-details" rel="nofollow">apiResponse.security_details()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-apiresponse#api-response-server-addr" rel="nofollow">apiResponse.server_addr()</a> mirror the browser-side <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-response#response-security-details" rel="nofollow">response.security_details()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-response#response-server-addr" rel="nofollow">response.server_addr()</a>.</li>
<li>New option <code>artifacts_dir</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-connect-over-cdp" rel="nofollow">browserType.connect_over_cdp()</a> controls where artifacts such as traces and downloads are stored when attached to an existing browser.</li>
<li>New option <code>cursor</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-actions" rel="nofollow">screencast.show_actions()</a> controls the cursor decoration rendered for pointer actions.</li>
<li>The <code>on_frame</code> callback in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-start" rel="nofollow">screencast.start()</a> now receives a <code>timestamp</code> of when the frame was presented by the browser.</li>
</ul>
<h2>🛠️ Other improvements</h2>
<ul>
<li>Playwright now supports Ubuntu 26.04.</li>
<li>HAR and trace recordings now include WebSocket requests.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Browser Versions</h2>
<ul>
<li>Chromium 149.0.7827.55</li>
<li>Mozilla Firefox 151.0</li>
<li>WebKit 26.5</li>
</ul>
<p>This version was also tested against the following stable channels:</p>
<ul>
<li>Google Chrome 149</li>
<li>Microsoft Edge 149</li>
</ul></content>

    <id>tag:github.com,2008:Repository/276414382/v1.60.0</id>
    <updated>2026-05-18T11:25:27Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-python/releases/tag/v1.60.0"/>
    <title>v1.60.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>🐍 Python improvements</h2>
<ul>
<li>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-formdata" rel="nofollow">FormData</a> class for building multipart/form-data request bodies — pass to <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext#api-request-context-post" rel="nofollow">api_request_context.post(form=…)</a> etc.</li>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/test-assertions#soft-assertions" rel="nofollow">expect.soft(...)</a> soft assertions collect multiple failures in a test instead of stopping at the first one. Requires up-to-date pytest integration to work.</li>
<li>All <code>timeout</code> parameters now accept <code>datetime.timedelta</code> — applies wherever a timeout is taken, e.g. <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-goto" rel="nofollow">page.goto()</a>, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-click" rel="nofollow">locator.click()</a>, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locatorassertions#locator-assertions-to-be-visible" rel="nofollow">expect(...).to_be_visible()</a>.</li>
<li>Async context manager support across more APIs — <code>async with</code> now works for objects returned from <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-actions" rel="nofollow">screencast.show_actions()</a>, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-overlays" rel="nofollow">screencast.show_overlays()</a>, etc.</li>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-wait-for-request" rel="nofollow">page.expect_request(...)</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-wait-for-response" rel="nofollow">page.expect_response(...)</a> now accept async predicates.</li>
<li>Typed overloads for <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-wait-for-event" rel="nofollow">expect_event</a> / <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-wait-for-event-2" rel="nofollow">wait_for_event</a> so the event payload type is inferred per event name.</li>
</ul>
<h2>🌐 HAR recording on Tracing</h2>
<p><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-start-har" rel="nofollow">tracing.start_har()</a> / <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-stop-har" rel="nofollow">tracing.stop_har()</a> expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same <code>content</code>, <code>mode</code> and <code>url_filter</code> options as <code>record_har</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="context.tracing.start_har(&quot;trace.har&quot;)
page = context.new_page()
page.goto(&quot;https://playwright.dev&quot;)
context.tracing.stop_har()"><pre><span class="pl-s1">context</span>.<span class="pl-c1">tracing</span>.<span class="pl-c1">start_har</span>(<span class="pl-s">"trace.har"</span>)
<span class="pl-s1">page</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">context</span>.<span class="pl-c1">new_page</span>()
<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">goto</span>(<span class="pl-s">"https://playwright.dev"</span>)
<span class="pl-s1">context</span>.<span class="pl-c1">tracing</span>.<span class="pl-c1">stop_har</span>()</pre></div>
<h2>🪝 Drop API</h2>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-drop" rel="nofollow">locator.drop()</a> simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches <code>dragenter</code>, <code>dragover</code>, and <code>drop</code> with a synthetic <code>DataTransfer</code> in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.locator(&quot;#dropzone&quot;).drop(
    files={&quot;name&quot;: &quot;note.txt&quot;, &quot;mime_type&quot;: &quot;text/plain&quot;, &quot;buffer&quot;: b&quot;hello&quot;},
)

page.locator(&quot;#dropzone&quot;).drop(
    data={
        &quot;text/plain&quot;: &quot;hello world&quot;,
        &quot;text/uri-list&quot;: &quot;https://example.com&quot;,
    },
)"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">locator</span>(<span class="pl-s">"#dropzone"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">drop</span>(
    <span class="pl-s1">files</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>{<span class="pl-s">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"note.txt"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"mime_type"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"text/plain"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"buffer"</span>: <span class="pl-s">b"hello"</span>},
)

<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">locator</span>(<span class="pl-s">"#dropzone"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">drop</span>(
    <span class="pl-s1">data</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>{
        <span class="pl-s">"text/plain"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"hello world"</span>,
        <span class="pl-s">"text/uri-list"</span>: <span class="pl-s">"https://example.com"</span>,
    },
)</pre></div>
<h2>🎯 Aria snapshots</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-pageassertions#page-assertions-to-match-aria-snapshot" rel="nofollow">expect(page).to_match_aria_snapshot()</a> now works on a <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page" rel="nofollow">Page</a>, in addition to a <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator" rel="nofollow">Locator</a> — equivalent to asserting against <code>page.locator("body")</code>.</li>
<li>New <code>boxes</code> option on <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-aria-snapshot" rel="nofollow">locator.aria_snapshot()</a> / <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-aria-snapshot" rel="nofollow">page.aria_snapshot()</a> appends each element's bounding box as <code>[box=x,y,width,height]</code>, useful for AI consumption.</li>
</ul>
<h2>New APIs</h2>
<h3>Browser, Context and Page</h3>
<ul>
<li>Event <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-event-context" rel="nofollow">browser.on("context")</a> — fired when a new context is created on the browser.</li>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext" rel="nofollow">BrowserContext</a> now mirrors lifecycle events from its pages: <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-download" rel="nofollow">browser_context.on("download")</a>, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-frame-attached" rel="nofollow">browser_context.on("frameattached")</a>, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-frame-detached" rel="nofollow">browser_context.on("framedetached")</a>, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-frame-navigated" rel="nofollow">browser_context.on("framenavigated")</a>, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-page-close" rel="nofollow">browser_context.on("pageclose")</a>, <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-page-load" rel="nofollow">browser_context.on("pageload")</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Locators and Assertions</h3>
<ul>
<li>New option <code>description</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-role" rel="nofollow">page.get_by_role()</a> / <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-get-by-role" rel="nofollow">locator.get_by_role()</a> / <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-frame#frame-get-by-role" rel="nofollow">frame.get_by_role()</a> / <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-framelocator#frame-locator-get-by-role" rel="nofollow">frame_locator.get_by_role()</a> for matching the <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#dfn-accessible-description" rel="nofollow">accessible description</a>.</li>
<li>New option <code>pseudo</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locatorassertions#locator-assertions-to-have-css" rel="nofollow">expect(locator).to_have_css()</a> reads computed styles from <code>::before</code> or <code>::after</code>.</li>
<li>New option <code>style</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-highlight" rel="nofollow">locator.highlight()</a> applies extra inline CSS to the highlight overlay, plus new <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-hide-highlight" rel="nofollow">page.hide_highlight()</a> to clear all highlights.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Network</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-websocketroute#web-socket-route-protocols" rel="nofollow">web_socket_route.protocols()</a> returns the WebSocket subprotocols requested by the page.</li>
<li>New option <code>no_defaults</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-connect-over-cdp" rel="nofollow">browser_type.connect_over_cdp()</a> disables Playwright's default overrides on the default context (download behavior, focus emulation, media emulation), so attaching to a user's daily-driver browser doesn't disturb its state.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Errors</h3>
<ul>
<li>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-weberror#web-error-location" rel="nofollow">web_error.location()</a> mirrors <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-consolemessage#console-message-location" rel="nofollow">console_message.location()</a>.</li>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-consolemessage#console-message-location" rel="nofollow">console_message.location()</a> now exposes <code>line</code> / <code>column</code> properties (<code>line_number</code> / <code>column_number</code> are deprecated).</li>
</ul>
<h2>🛠️ Other improvements</h2>
<ul>
<li>Trace Viewer adds a pretty-print toggle for JSON / form request and response bodies in the network details panel.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Breaking Changes <g-emoji class="g-emoji" alias="warning">⚠️</g-emoji></h2>
<ul>
<li>Removed long-deprecated <code>handle</code> option on <code>browser_context.expose_binding()</code> and <code>page.expose_binding()</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Browser Versions</h2>
<ul>
<li>Chromium 148.0.7778.96</li>
<li>Mozilla Firefox 150.0.2</li>
<li>WebKit 26.4</li>
</ul>
<p>This version was also tested against the following stable channels:</p>
<ul>
<li>Google Chrome 147</li>
<li>Microsoft Edge 147</li>
</ul></content>

    <id>tag:github.com,2008:Repository/276414382/v1.59.0</id>
    <updated>2026-04-29T07:37:58Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-python/releases/tag/v1.59.0"/>
    <title>v1.59.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>🎬 Screencast</h2>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-screencast" rel="nofollow">page.screencast</a> API provides a unified interface for capturing page content with:</p>
<ul>
<li>Screencast recordings</li>
<li>Action annotations</li>
<li>Visual overlays</li>
<li>Real-time frame capture</li>
<li>Agentic video receipts</li>
</ul>

<p><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/playwright/main/docs/src/images/release-notes-1.59-screencast-demo.gif"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/playwright/main/docs/src/images/release-notes-1.59-screencast-demo.gif" alt="Demo" width="500" height="313" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; max-height: 313px;"></a></p>

<p><strong>Screencast recording</strong> — record video with precise start/stop control, as an alternative to the <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context-option-record-video-dir" rel="nofollow"><code>recordVideoDir</code></a> option:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.screencast.start(path=&quot;video.webm&quot;)
# ... perform actions ...
page.screencast.stop()"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">start</span>(<span class="pl-s1">path</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"video.webm"</span>)
<span class="pl-c"># ... perform actions ...</span>
<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">stop</span>()</pre></div>
<p><strong>Action annotations</strong> — enable built-in visual annotations that highlight interacted elements and display action titles during recording:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.screencast.show_actions(position=&quot;top-right&quot;)"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">show_actions</span>(<span class="pl-s1">position</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"top-right"</span>)</pre></div>
<p><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-actions" rel="nofollow">screencast.show_actions()</a> accepts <code>position</code> (<code>'top-left'</code>, <code>'top'</code>, <code>'top-right'</code>, <code>'bottom-left'</code>, <code>'bottom'</code>, <code>'bottom-right'</code>), <code>duration</code> (ms per annotation), and <code>font_size</code> (px). Returns a disposable to stop showing actions.</p>
<p><strong>Visual overlays</strong> — add chapter titles and custom HTML overlays on top of the page for richer narration:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.screencast.show_chapter(&quot;Adding TODOs&quot;,
    description=&quot;Type and press enter for each TODO&quot;,
    duration=1000,
)

page.screencast.show_overlay('&lt;div style=&quot;color: red&quot;&gt;Recording&lt;/div&gt;')"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">show_chapter</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Adding TODOs"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">description</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"Type and press enter for each TODO"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">duration</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">1000</span>,
)

<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">show_overlay</span>(<span class="pl-s">'&lt;div style="color: red"&gt;Recording&lt;/div&gt;'</span>)</pre></div>
<p><strong>Real-time frame capture</strong> — stream JPEG-encoded frames for custom processing like thumbnails, live previews, AI vision, and more:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.screencast.start(
    on_frame=lambda frame: send_to_vision_model(frame[&quot;data&quot;]),
)"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">start</span>(
    <span class="pl-s1">on_frame</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-k">lambda</span> <span class="pl-s1">frame</span>: <span class="pl-en">send_to_vision_model</span>(<span class="pl-s1">frame</span>[<span class="pl-s">"data"</span>]),
)</pre></div>
<p><strong>Agentic video receipts</strong> — coding agents can produce video evidence of their work. After completing a task, an agent can record a walkthrough video with rich annotations for human review:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="page.screencast.start(path=&quot;receipt.webm&quot;)
page.screencast.show_actions(position=&quot;top-right&quot;)

page.screencast.show_chapter(&quot;Verifying checkout flow&quot;,
    description=&quot;Added coupon code support per ticket #1234&quot;,
)

# Agent performs the verification steps...
page.locator(&quot;#coupon&quot;).fill(&quot;SAVE20&quot;)
page.locator(&quot;#apply-coupon&quot;).click()
expect(page.locator(&quot;.discount&quot;)).to_contain_text(&quot;20%&quot;)

page.screencast.show_chapter(&quot;Done&quot;,
    description=&quot;Coupon applied, discount reflected in total&quot;,
)

page.screencast.stop()"><pre><span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">start</span>(<span class="pl-s1">path</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"receipt.webm"</span>)
<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">show_actions</span>(<span class="pl-s1">position</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"top-right"</span>)

<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">show_chapter</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Verifying checkout flow"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">description</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"Added coupon code support per ticket #1234"</span>,
)

<span class="pl-c"># Agent performs the verification steps...</span>
<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">locator</span>(<span class="pl-s">"#coupon"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">fill</span>(<span class="pl-s">"SAVE20"</span>)
<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">locator</span>(<span class="pl-s">"#apply-coupon"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">click</span>()
<span class="pl-en">expect</span>(<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">locator</span>(<span class="pl-s">".discount"</span>)).<span class="pl-c1">to_contain_text</span>(<span class="pl-s">"20%"</span>)

<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">show_chapter</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Done"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">description</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"Coupon applied, discount reflected in total"</span>,
)

<span class="pl-s1">page</span>.<span class="pl-c1">screencast</span>.<span class="pl-c1">stop</span>()</pre></div>
<p>The resulting video serves as a receipt: chapter titles provide context, action annotations highlight each interaction, and the visual walkthrough is faster to review than text logs.</p>
<h2>🔍 Snapshots and Locators</h2>
<ul>
<li>Method <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-aria-snapshot" rel="nofollow">page.aria_snapshot()</a> to capture the aria snapshot of the page — equivalent to <code>page.locator('body').aria_snapshot()</code>.</li>
<li>Options <code>depth</code> and <code>mode</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-aria-snapshot" rel="nofollow">locator.aria_snapshot()</a>.</li>
<li>Method <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-normalize" rel="nofollow">locator.normalize()</a> converts a locator to follow best practices like test ids and aria roles.</li>
<li>Method <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-pick-locator" rel="nofollow">page.pick_locator()</a> enters an interactive mode where hovering over elements highlights them and shows the corresponding locator. Click an element to get its <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator" rel="nofollow">Locator</a> back. Use <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-cancel-pick-locator" rel="nofollow">page.cancel_pick_locator()</a> to cancel.</li>
</ul>
<h2>New APIs</h2>
<h3>Screencast</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-screencast" rel="nofollow">page.screencast</a> provides video recording, real-time frame streaming, and overlay management.</li>
<li>Methods <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-start" rel="nofollow">screencast.start()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-stop" rel="nofollow">screencast.stop()</a> for recording and frame capture.</li>
<li>Methods <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-actions" rel="nofollow">screencast.show_actions()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-hide-actions" rel="nofollow">screencast.hide_actions()</a> for action annotations.</li>
<li>Methods <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-chapter" rel="nofollow">screencast.show_chapter()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-overlay" rel="nofollow">screencast.show_overlay()</a> for visual overlays.</li>
<li>Methods <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-show-overlays" rel="nofollow">screencast.show_overlays()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-screencast#screencast-hide-overlays" rel="nofollow">screencast.hide_overlays()</a> for overlay visibility control.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Storage, Console and Errors</h3>
<ul>
<li>Method <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-set-storage-state" rel="nofollow">browser_context.set_storage_state()</a> clears existing cookies, local storage, and IndexedDB for all origins and sets a new storage state — no need to create a new context.</li>
<li>Methods <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-clear-console-messages" rel="nofollow">page.clear_console_messages()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-clear-page-errors" rel="nofollow">page.clear_page_errors()</a> to clear stored messages and errors.</li>
<li>Option <code>filter</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-console-messages" rel="nofollow">page.console_messages()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-page#page-page-errors" rel="nofollow">page.page_errors()</a> controls which messages are returned.</li>
<li>Method <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-consolemessage#console-message-timestamp" rel="nofollow">console_message.timestamp()</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Miscellaneous</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-debugger" rel="nofollow">browser_context.debugger</a> provides programmatic control over the Playwright debugger.</li>
<li>Method <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-is-closed" rel="nofollow">browser_context.is_closed()</a>.</li>
<li>Method <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-request#request-existing-response" rel="nofollow">request.existing_response()</a> returns the response without waiting.</li>
<li>Method <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-response#response-http-version" rel="nofollow">response.http_version()</a> returns the HTTP version used by the response.</li>
<li>Option <code>live</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-start" rel="nofollow">tracing.start()</a> for real-time trace updates.</li>
<li>Option <code>artifacts_dir</code> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-launch" rel="nofollow">browser_type.launch()</a> to configure the artifacts directory.</li>
</ul>
<h2>🔗 Interoperability</h2>
<p>New <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-bind" rel="nofollow">browser.bind()</a> API makes a launched browser available for <code>playwright-cli</code>, <code>@playwright/mcp</code>, and other clients to connect to.</p>
<p><strong>Bind a browser</strong> — start a browser and bind it so others can connect:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="server_info = await browser.bind(&quot;my-session&quot;,
    workspace_dir=&quot;/my/project&quot;,
)"><pre><span class="pl-s1">server_info</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-s1">browser</span>.<span class="pl-c1">bind</span>(<span class="pl-s">"my-session"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">workspace_dir</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"/my/project"</span>,
)</pre></div>
<p><strong>Connect from playwright-cli</strong> — connect to the running browser from your favorite coding agent.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="playwright-cli attach my-session
playwright-cli -s my-session snapshot"><pre>playwright-cli attach my-session
playwright-cli -s my-session snapshot</pre></div>
<p><strong>Connect from @playwright/mcp</strong> — or point your MCP server to the running browser.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="@playwright/mcp --endpoint=my-session"><pre>@playwright/mcp --endpoint=my-session</pre></div>
<p><strong>Connect from a Playwright client</strong> — use API to connect to the browser. Multiple clients at a time are supported!</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="browser = await chromium.connect(server_info[&quot;endpoint&quot;])"><pre><span class="pl-s1">browser</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-s1">chromium</span>.<span class="pl-c1">connect</span>(<span class="pl-s1">server_info</span>[<span class="pl-s">"endpoint"</span>])</pre></div>
<p>Pass <code>host</code> and <code>port</code> options to bind over WebSocket instead of a named pipe:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="server_info = await browser.bind(&quot;my-session&quot;,
    host=&quot;localhost&quot;,
    port=0,
)
# server_info[&quot;endpoint&quot;] is a ws:// URL"><pre><span class="pl-s1">server_info</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-k">await</span> <span class="pl-s1">browser</span>.<span class="pl-c1">bind</span>(<span class="pl-s">"my-session"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">host</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">"localhost"</span>,
    <span class="pl-s1">port</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">0</span>,
)
<span class="pl-c"># server_info["endpoint"] is a ws:// URL</span></pre></div>
<p>Call <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-unbind" rel="nofollow">browser.unbind()</a> to stop accepting new connections.</p>
<h2>📊 Observability</h2>
<p>Run <code>playwright-cli show</code> to open the Dashboard that lists all the bound browsers, their statuses, and allows interacting with them:</p>
<ul>
<li>See what your agent is doing on the background browsers</li>
<li>Click into the sessions for manual interventions</li>
<li>Open DevTools to inspect pages from the background browsers.</li>
</ul>

<p><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/playwright/main/docs/src/images/release-notes-1.59-dashboard.png"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/playwright/main/docs/src/images/release-notes-1.59-dashboard.png" alt="Demo" width="1169" height="835" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; max-height: 835px;"></a></p>

    <title>v1.58.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>Trace Viewer Improvements</h2>
<ul>
<li>New 'system' theme option follows your OS dark/light mode preference</li>
<li>Search functionality (Cmd/Ctrl+F) is now available in code editors</li>
<li>Network details panel has been reorganized for better usability</li>
<li>JSON responses are now automatically formatted for readability</li>
</ul>
<p>Thanks to <a href="https://github.com/cpAdm">@cpAdm</a> for contributing these improvements!</p>
<h2>Miscellaneous</h2>
<p><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-connect-over-cdp" rel="nofollow">browser_type.connect_over_cdp()</a> now accepts an <code>is_local</code> option. When set to <code>True</code>, it tells Playwright that it runs on the same host as the CDP server, enabling file system optimizations.</p>

<li>Removed <code>_react</code> and <code>_vue</code> selectors. See <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/locators" rel="nofollow">locators guide</a> for alternatives.</li>
<li>Removed <code>:light</code> selector engine suffix. Use standard CSS selectors instead.</li>
<li>Option <code>devtools</code> from <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-launch" rel="nofollow">browser_type.launch()</a> has been removed. Use <code>args=['--auto-open-devtools-for-tabs']</code> instead.</li>

</ul>

<li>Chromium 145.0.7632.6</li>
<li>Mozilla Firefox 146.0.1</li>
<li>WebKit 26.0</li>
</ul>
<p>This version was also tested against the following stable channels:</p>
<ul>
<li>Google Chrome 144</li>
<li>Microsoft Edge 144</li>
</ul></content>

    <title>v1.57.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h2>Chrome for Testing</h2>
<p>Starting with this release, Playwright switches from Chromium, to using <a href="https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing/" rel="nofollow">Chrome for Testing</a> builds. Both headed and headless browsers are subject to this. Your tests should still be passing after upgrading to Playwright 1.57.</p>
<p>We're expecting no functional changes to come from this switch. The biggest change is the new icon and title in your toolbar.</p>
<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/14912729/518586000-e9a5c4f2-9f35-4c27-9382-0f5eda377097.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..oTXFdhOjQrxKpU6eu1W3yNdCX7W-Ln-Wjg7tdYv-bZE"><img width="500" alt="new and old logo" src="https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/14912729/518586000-e9a5c4f2-9f35-4c27-9382-0f5eda377097.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..oTXFdhOjQrxKpU6eu1W3yNdCX7W-Ln-Wjg7tdYv-bZE" content-type-secured-asset="image/png" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<p>If you still see an unexpected behaviour change, please <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/new">file an issue</a>.</p>
<p>On Arm64 Linux, Playwright continues to use Chromium.</p>
<h2>Breaking Change</h2>
<p>After 3 years of being deprecated, we removed <code>page.accessibility</code> from our API. Please use other libraries such as <a href="https://www.deque.com/axe/" rel="nofollow">Axe</a> if you need to test page accessibility. See our Node.js <a href="https://playwright.dev/docs/accessibility-testing" rel="nofollow">guide</a> for integration with Axe.</p>
<h2>New APIs</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-worker#worker-event-console" rel="nofollow">worker.on("console")</a> event is emitted when JavaScript within the worker calls one of console API methods, e.g. console.log or console.dir. <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-worker#worker-wait-for-event" rel="nofollow">worker.expect_event()</a> can be used to wait for it.</li>
<li><a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-description" rel="nofollow">locator.description()</a> returns locator description previously set with <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-describe" rel="nofollow">locator.describe()</a>.</li>
<li>New option <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-click-option-steps" rel="nofollow"><code>steps</code></a> in <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-click" rel="nofollow">locator.click()</a> and <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-locator#locator-drag-to" rel="nofollow">locator.drag_to()</a> that configures the number of <code>mousemove</code> events emitted while moving the mouse pointer to the target element.</li>
<li>Network requests issued by <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/service-workers#network-events-and-routing" rel="nofollow">Service Workers</a> are now reported and can be routed through the <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-browsercontext" rel="nofollow">BrowserContext</a>, only in Chromium. You can opt out using the <code>PLAYWRIGHT_DISABLE_SERVICE_WORKER_NETWORK</code> environment variable.</li>
<li>Console messages from Service Workers are dispatched through <a href="https://playwright.dev/python/docs/api/class-worker#worker-event-console" rel="nofollow">worker.on("console")</a>. You can opt out of this using the <code>PLAYWRIGHT_DISABLE_SERVICE_WORKER_CONSOLE</code> environment variable.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Browser Versions</h2>
<ul>
<li>Chromium 143.0.7499.4</li>
<li>Mozilla Firefox 144.0.2</li>
<li>WebKit 26.0</li>
</ul></content>
